name: Todrah
confidence_why: 2 independent first-hand descriptions agree (1 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed-dominant, rule 01: unstressed presyllable + stressed main syllable) rests on an explicit statement in the only existing phonological description of Todrah, a 1973 primary-fieldwork article by SIL phonologists; the quotation was verified verbatim at p.145 in the PDF downloaded this compilation (previously not yet obtained held by the project). Glottolog lists exactly one descriptive reference for the languoid and web searches found no newer grammar, phonology or instrumental study, so no better source exists that could change the classification; the iambic sesquisyllabic pattern is also what the authors state for all neighboring North Bahnaric languages. Only housekeeping suggested: point the record's 'held' field at list of works to obtain is empty because nothing unheld would improve the record.

sources.citation: Gregerson & Smith 1973, The development of Todrah register, Mon-Khmer Studies 4:143-184, p. 145 (Internet Archive copy of sealang.net PDF, page scan read)
sources.quote: The Todrah word pattern resembles that of the neighboring North Bahnaric languages having optionally an unstressed open presyllable with a schwa vowel and a stressed main syllable consisting of an initial consonant or consonant cluster, vowel and an optional final consonant.

sources.citation: Gregerson, Kenneth J. & Kenneth D. Smith. 1973. The development of Tơdrah register. Mon-Khmer Studies 4:143-184.
sources.quote: 'The Tơdrah word pattern resembles that of the neighboring North Bahnaric languages having optionally an unstressed open presyllable with a schwa vowel and a stressed main syllable consisting of an initial consonant or consonant cluster, vowel and an optional final consonant.'

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1972. A phonological reconstruction of Proto-North-Bahnaric. Language Data, Asian-Pacific Series 2. Santa Ana: SIL (1977 Manila reprint), 117 pp. (SIL archive item 4194, via Internet Archive copy 2022-10-08)
sources.quote: Comparative work; Todrah (Modra and Didra) is named only as a language 'referred to' alongside the five reconstruction languages (p.1); word form given as (Cə)CVC (p.3). No Todrah-specific stress statement found in the pages read.
